2026-05-14_164438.webp.description: Day 1 of the trip. Reached Ya'an after a 130km ride from Chengdu.

2026-05-15_182949.webp.description: An obelisk in Xingou, a small village in the mountains where I stayed overnight. The owner of the hostel is known among cyclists as a good cook.

2026-05-16_121256.webp.description: After the Erlang Mountain Tunnel, the snow peaks are now visible in the distance.

2026-05-16_190204.webp.description: Luding Bridge over the Dadu River, a significant historical site from the Long March of the Red Army. Behind it is the newly built expressway bridge.

2026-05-17_135649.webp.description: Looking back before the tunnel. Road signs warning of slippery conditions, continuous downhill (which I just climbed up), and high traffic accident risk.

2026-05-17_210400.webp.description: Kangding city at night, known for traditional folk songs.

2026-05-19_112630.webp.description: Winding snowy roads going up to Zheduo Mountain Pass, the first high pass of the G318 at 4298m. It's said that anyone who can cycle up this pass can finish the whole G318 (not true).

2026-05-19_162900.webp.description: Descending from Zheduo Mountain. The last few kilometres of climb to the top took me ages, and gave me a muscle injury so bad that I could barely walk that night. It was my first time cycling at such high altitude.

2026-05-21_125301.webp.description: Grassland from Xinduqiao to Tagong, an 80km recovery ride. I ate dumplings halfway, which had to be cooked in a pressure cooker at this altitude.

2026-05-21_142801.webp.description: Buddhist murals on rocks near Tagong.

2026-05-21_155537.webp.description: Tagong Monastery. Local legend says that when Princess Wencheng was travelling to Tibet, the life-sized statue of a twelve-year-old Shakyamuni Buddha she was carrying became immovable here until a replica was left behind. Tibetans believe that if you cannot make the pilgrimage all the way to Lhasa, worshipping at Tagong Monastery yields the exact same spiritual merit.

2026-05-21_194016.webp.description: A monastery on a small hill near where I stayed in Xinduqiao.

2026-05-22_133501.webp.description: Yajiang's spiral overpass, a 300m vertical drop in just 8km (almost got scraped by a lorry here).

2026-05-23_112241.webp.description: The 3000km road sign of the G318, filled with messages from cyclists. This stretch is the steepest 10km of the journey, averaging about 9-10% gradient.

2026-05-23_205337.webp.description: Three Sisters Hostel at Xiangkezong, a well-known pit stop for cyclists, motorcyclists, and backpackers. Its walls are filled with messages left by travellers.

2026-05-24_114951.webp.description: Me after climbing up the Eighteen Bends of the Sky Road (天路十八弯). Now 4000m is the baseline altitude I'm cycling at.

2026-05-25_130524.webp.description: Yak sign on the way to Litang.

2026-05-25_192000.webp.description: Changqingchun Ke'er Monastery under the afternoon sun.

2026-05-27_080411.webp.description: Messages left behind by travellers on the wall of a hostel in Heni.

2026-05-27_122100.webp.description: Fellow cyclist near the top of Haizi Mountain, 4685m above sea level.

2026-05-27_131200.webp.description: One of the best views of the trip.
